id: # lane/rerender: the stale render recordings re-recorded on today's oracle; what their replays and re-recordings found

cause: WorldProviderEnd.getFogColor: native wrote the green channel as the literal 0.50196078f, an ulp below Java's 128 / 255.0F, so every End frame's fog green was an ulp low; the old te_portal_end predates the cs rows whose camera check compares it

not a regression: the goldens were drawn at partial tick 1.0 then 0.5 and the second draw moves the next frame (the pickup flight); coverage replayed the frames at 1.0 only and diverged at t=26 on every build since the recording. The oracle now draws --frame-pts' later ticks without writing PNGs and coverage.sh passes --frame-pts 1.0,0.5 for such tapes

one of four fresh recordings of the te_portal_end script (SceneSetup into the End at t=2) had 143 server entities at t=2 where the other three and the 2026-09-26 recording have 146 (d.ents, d.sw, d.sseed differ from t=2 on); the End's spawn after a dimension change is not reproducible under load
repro: record rendertick/te_portal_end_rr/script.jsonl several times at load 200 and compare w.ents at t=2

cause: master's coverage replayed render/worldfx_underwater on pool member 26 and got a different last frame (t=25, printed after ORACLE REPLAY OK); fresh JVMs on ba67044f and e6a11497 and another pool member replay it OK, so a member's earlier job leaks into the frame
repro: make -C oracle coverage RECS=render/worldfx_underwater on a warm pool after the other rs- scenes (out/java/coverage/logs/rs-worldfx_underwater.log on master)

cause: render/terrain1 (render distance 8, fancy, mipmaps) replays OK on 111a53f7, 9d0030f7 and cc15352b but diverges at t=81 d.px on 187ed4ff, 7ed4c366, b96f3ab1, d198ec49, d57f07fe, a28540af and c996bbc6: its frame follows timing (at render distance 8 even two fresh recordings list RenderGlobal's tile entities in different orders)
repro: replay out/java/render/terrain1 fresh several times under load
